Top 36-pct PAYE tax threshold to be raised above 500,000 rupees: President
The income threshold for the top 36 percent Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) tax bracket will be raised beyond 500,000 rupees in the coming year or the year after next, Sri Lanka President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said.

Mixed 3Q for banks: Core earnings held up, profits declined; margins expected to remain flat

Sri Lanka's big four banks (COMB, HNB, NTB and SAMP) delivered a mixed 3Q26. NII and fee income grew, while asset quality improved. However, mark-to-market and forex losses of around LKR 17.8bn weighed on profitability, driving an average 24% Q/Q decline in profits. Loan growth moderated to an average of 4.9% as banks became more selective, despite firm credit demand.

Looking ahead, we expect NIMs to remain broadly flat over the next six months, with limited repricing from the latest 25bps rate hike, while credit growth is likely to moderate further.
